items.title: Top-earning Australians make money very differently from typical workers
items.description: In Australia, the way people earn their money affects the rate of tax they pay — and top earners have a very different income mix from everyone else.

items.title: Spain's Tenerife port prepares for arrival of hantavirus-hit cruise ship
items.description: The Centers for Disease Control is now involved in managing the outbreak of hantavirus aboard the MV Hondius, which is set to arrive this afternoon in the Canary Islands.

items.title: Missing scientists may represent a 'grave threat to US national security'
items.description: The scientists supposedly all had access to sensitive government research, and the nature of their work has led to speculation that their cases might all be connected.

items.title: Chalmers reveals gas tax revenue is up in federal budget
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers says the tax on offshore gas projects has raised more revenue than expected this year, as he prepares to hand down a budget focused on fixing a "broken" housing market and tax system.

items.title: Why this ex-Liberal thinks she can unite One Nation and Greens voters
items.description: Charlotte Mortlock believes it is time for Australia to leave the left-right ideology behind and focus on what brings people together instead.

items.title: Pauline Hanson lashes 'arrogant' critics who say One Nation can't go mainstream
items.description: Pauline Hanson says the major parties "will lose" because of an "arrogant" belief that One Nation is not able to become a mainstream force, following the party's first lower house win this century.

items.title: Live: Demons too good for Eagles, Tigers hunting consecutive wins in Crows clash
items.description: Melbourne completes a routine victory over West Coast at Docklands, while Richmond, fresh from its first win of the year, welcomes Adelaide to the MCG. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Storm stun Tigers with scoring blitz but lose fullback to broken cheek
items.description: The Melbourne Storm is on a seven-match losing streak, the club's worst run since entering the NRL, and hosts Wests Tigers. Follow live.

items.title: I met the 'ISIS brides' on a flight to Australia
items.description: The "ISIS brides" have been stuck in a Syrian refugee camp for years but have now finally come back to Australia. ABC journalist Bridget Rollason sat a few seats away from them on the 13-hour flight to Melbourne and tells us what happened when they spoke.

items.title: 18-year-old man dies falling from sixth floor balcony while fleeing police
items.description: Police said the 18-year-old attempted to flee over the balcony when he fell and sustained critical injuries.

items.title: Man charged with gross indecency, rape after 'appalling behaviour' in hotel
items.description: NT Police have charged a 41-year-old man with rape after his "appalling behaviour" inside a hotel room, which authorities allege was one of two domestic violence incidents to occur in Darwin's CBD in the same day.

items.title: John Polson was headed for jail. One phone call changed his life forever
items.description: John Polson was a troubled teen when a sliding doors moment led him into the world of acting. He went on to create Tropfest, one of the world's biggest short film festivals, changing his life and the Australian industry.

items.title: Premier backs away from revealing reasons for backbencher's legal costs
items.description: Tasmania's premier is under fire for backtracking on an undertaking to explain why taxpayers paid a $15,000 legal bill for a backbencher.

items.title: Person dies after being hit by plane in the US
items.description: A person who jumped a fence at a US airport has been killed after being struck by a plane during take-off.

items.title: Love when you don't know how long you've got
items.description: My 14-year-old daughter Pip has Williams syndrome. The future is uncertain and full of heartache, but my love for my baby is not.

items.title: An old Australian classic story is getting a new operatic treatment
items.description: Leah Purcell’s The Drover’s Wife is being transformed into an opera with music by George Palmer and starring soprano Nina Korbe.

items.title: 'My career wasn't the same': Why Kira Puru stopped releasing songs
items.description: Kira Puru is known for their triple j Hottest 100-charting energetic pop music, but this year the musician has roles in not one, but two of the biggest Australian TV shows. What's behind the pivot?

items.title: We asked the IRGC for their Strait of Hormuz rules and they emailed us back
items.description: Amid a fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran, the IRGC has launched a maritime authority for the Strait of Hormuz. The Persian Gulf Strait Authority says ships need to email their application for passage. So, we sent them a request.

items.title: Sunwater chair labels costly dam rebuild 'grossly disproportionate'
items.description: In a letter addressed to the water minister, Sunwater chair Jeff Seeney said the decision to rebuild the dam lacked "any rigour" or "professional credibility".

items.title: Police questioning fail-to-stop driver after 92yo killed in crash
items.description: A car rolled and smashed into a power pole, killing its elderly passenger, after swerving to avoid a car driving the wrong way on the New England Highway in southern Queensland.

items.title: Climbers winched to safety after overnight ordeal in the Warrumbungles
items.description: A falling rock sparks a tense rescue in the Warrumbungle National Park in central-western New South Wales.

items.title: Alexa Leary misses out on Commonwealth Games after reclassification
items.description: Alexa Leary is classified out of the Commonwealth Games team as Swimming Australia names first half of squad for Glasgow 2026.

items.title: One woman calls it 'potato brain'. She's among half of the workforce with burnout
items.description: Burnout is everywhere — in resignation letters, therapy sessions and late-night emails. Yet the debate over what it is reveals a bigger question: Should workplaces bear responsibility for the damage modern work can cause?

items.title: Who is responsible for the problems in Alice Springs town camps?
items.description: Conditions in town camps in Alice Springs are under intense scrutiny, but the residents are caught in a tangled web of bureaucracy with little transparency on the money being spent and who exactly is responsible for what.

items.title: 'A terrible waste': Prison unit barely used amid overcrowding crisis
items.description: The notorious Unit 18, a makeshift youth detention facility within the adult Casuarina Prison, has sat empty for at least a week while other WA prisons are bursting at the seams.
